event.summary: Zero-valued Trash fixture leaves a decoder assertion gap, without a demonstrated product defect
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 06d4b68f3a9e913f47cd426fedee5946a4eed77b. TLDR: Considered whether the newly added Trash change counter could silently fail to reach browsers because every shared fixture row sets it to zero. Source/contract: helm http_contract_tests.rs:119-140 sets trash_epoch: 0; UI api/http_contract_tests.rs:163-249 checks host metadata but does not assert trash_epoch; UI lib.rs:824-827 explicitly declares #[serde(default)] pub trash_epoch: u64 under the same JSON name, while helm hosts.rs:121-123 serializes pub(crate) trash_epoch: u64. SPEC_impl.md:495-501 describes shared golden files preventing HTTP mirrors from drifting. The zero fixture cannot distinguish a correct decode from a default, so a future rename would escape this particular assertion, but current source has matching names and types. Suggested bucket: other (test coverage only). Confidence: confirmed source-level test limitation; no current user-visible failure established. proposed_drop: do not report a product defect; the current decoder is explicitly present with the matching name/type at lib.rs:824-827. possible_cover: none searched. Could-be-highest: no; this candidate concerns test discrimination, not an established destructive or security route. Caveat: no runtime tests or reproductions performed; adjacent Trash refresh behavior remains outside this group's primary patch scope.

event.summary: The new Trash epoch golden fixture cannot detect a defaulted decoder regression
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 06d4b68f3a9e913f47cd426fedee5946a4eed77b. TLDR: The fast HTTP contract tests do not protect the newly introduced value that tells idle windows when Trash changed; a browser decoder regression can pass them and leave idle Trash stale. This is a test-quality finding, not a claim that the current decoder is broken. Revision: promote c1 from candidate; retract its earlier proposed drop based on the currently matching name/type, because that does not refute a test's failure to distinguish a future decoder regression. Original consequence and source citations are retained here and in the original event. Exact sensitivity: the changed producer fixture assigns trash_epoch: 0 to every host (http_contract_tests.rs:119-140; corresponding host-list.json additions); UI lib.rs:824-827 declares a defaulted u64. A decoder serde rename while retaining the Rust member would decode the old JSON field as zero without affecting the rest of Host, and the complete consumer golden test (api/http_contract_tests.rs:163-321) never asserts trash_epoch. Producer equality still passes because the helm serializer did not change. Merely adding a zero-valued assertion would still not distinguish this regression: use a nonzero fixture value and assert that exact value in the browser mirror test. Contract: SPEC_impl.md:495-501 says shared golden files keep HTTP mirrors from drifting. The test module's explicit rationale at http_contract_tests.rs:10-18 says fields added/renamed should fail this pair, and specifically says 'an Option left at None or a defaulted field would let a rename of that field slip through both sides.' Attribution: this commit adds the field to both the HostView fixture and the golden JSON, so populating and asserting the new field is directly this patch's contract responsibility. Other coverage checked: sessions_tests.rs:1407-1416 checks the typed HostView counter after deletion; it does not serialize the host reply or decode it as the UI Host. All Rust UI occurrences of trash_epoch are its declaration, typed struct literals, or HostTrashReader's consumption at list/trash.rs:690-697; none supplies a nonzero JSON decoder assertion. Browser coverage does exist: e2e/tests/rail-notices.spec.ts:37-46 injects nonzero trash_epoch values, and :281-312 distinguishes idle per-host refresh; that coverage would catch a decoder rename if run. It does not fulfill the golden pair's independent fast Rust-test role: the module explains browser tests are where drift formerly surfaced and CI does not run them. Suggested bucket: other/test quality. Confidence: confirmed through source and assertion analysis; no tests or reproductions run. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: existing browser sensitivity noted above, not a claim that no test anywhere covers the behavior. Could-be-highest: no; this record establishes a test gap and potential stale Trash display, not security or work loss. Caveats: g022/f2's missing fleet wake after a particular delete ordering is a distinct product defect supplied by the caller; this record neither duplicates it nor claims to independently validate that ordering. Correct current field names/types remain a fact, but do not remove the sensitivity gap.

event.summary: Optional environment projection is absent from the golden host fixture
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 56659839785691f76da3af5d8f51b511cff4ba8b. TLDR: Considered whether setting environment to None in every golden host hides malformed container-host metadata from the HTTP contract tests. Source/contract: http_contract_tests.rs:119-142 adds environment: None; existing Tensorlake overrides at :239-264 do not populate it and no Podman row is added. hosts.rs:69-71 uses skip_serializing_if = Option::is_none, so this deliberately leaves the existing host-list fixture unchanged. hosts.rs:4260-4288 projects Tensorlake and Podman bindings into the shared farhelm_proto::EnvironmentHostView, whose explicit serde-derived fields are in crates/farhelm-proto/src/environment.rs:143-155. SPEC_impl.md Disposable environments, Environment rows and provider state states: 'Host views retain session-owned rows in Hosts, update tracking and ordinary attention.' The fixture therefore does not exercise the populated projection or Podman's host kind, but inspection establishes no serialization failure or unsafe behavior in this assigned one-line test change. Suggested bucket: other (fixture coverage). Confidence: confirmed source-level omission, no user-visible defect established. proposed_drop: do not report as a product bug; None is omitted by the production serializer at hosts.rs:69-71 and populated projections use the shared serde-derived type at environment.rs:143-155. possible_cover: none searched. Could-be-highest: no; no security or loss-of-work route follows from this fixture omission alone. Caveats: adjacent provider implementation and UI work belong to other groups; this is not a claim that their full implementations are correct. No tests or reproductions executed.

event.summary: The new environment host JSON is omitted from every golden contract row
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 56659839785691f76da3af5d8f51b511cff4ba8b. TLDR: The HTTP contract test gains the environment field but leaves its new serialized shape entirely untested, so changes to the environment key or populated resource metadata can pass the golden check. This is a concrete test-quality finding; it does not assert that the current serializer is malformed. Revision: promote c2 from candidate and retract the earlier proposed drop that cited a valid None serializer/shared serde type. Those facts explain why the golden omits the field; they do not make the test distinguish its populated schema. Original suspected consequence (malformed container-host metadata passing the HTTP contract tests), prior citations and proposed drop remain preserved in the original event. Source/attribution: this patch adds environment: None in host_list_body at http_contract_tests.rs:119-142. Every example, including Tensorlake overrides at :239-264, inherits None and no Podman row is present. Production HostView adds environment with skip_serializing_if = Option::is_none at hosts.rs:69-71; unlike the fixture, real host_views at :527-558 populates it, and the exhaustive HostKind projection at :4260-4288 produces Some for both Tensorlake and Podman bindings. EnvironmentHostView at crates/farhelm-proto/src/environment.rs:143-155 serializes name, place_name, target, tunnels and credential_warning. Concrete competing regression: adding a serde rename to HostView.environment, while retaining its Rust field and populated producer, changes actual GET /api/hosts JSON but changes neither the all-None fixture serialization nor host-list.json; host_list_serializes_to_the_shared_fixture (:317-325) still compares the same value. A nested serialized key/target representation change is similarly absent from this fixture. This is directly attributed to accommodating a new public field in the existing contract constructor without an example of its populated shape. Contract: module docs :10-18 explicitly call these files the HTTP contract and explain that fully populated options are needed to catch renames; SPEC_impl.md:495-501 describes the golden files' role. SPEC_impl.md Disposable environments, Environment rows and provider state says 'Host views retain session-owned rows in Hosts, update tracking and ordinary attention.' Other checks: git grep for EnvironmentHostView, environment_view calls and JSON environment access across crates/e2e at this revision found only the type, re-export, production declaration and projection; no populated serialization/assertion test was found. UI Host at this revision does not yet mirror the environment field, so this finding is narrowed to the producer golden's unpinned public schema; it does not invent an existing UI environment decoder regression. A populated Tensorlake/Podman golden example would pin the outer key and shared nested serialization; retain None on ordinary hosts to cover omission too. Suggested bucket: other/test quality. Confidence: confirmed by source and retained assertions; no tests or reproductions run. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none known; no forbidden coverage sources searched. Could-be-highest: no; the finding establishes test sensitivity, not an established destructive/security path. Caveats: shared serde types ensure Rust type compatibility, not stable JSON key names; adding a production projection integration assertion may be useful separately but the concrete in-scope gap does not depend on judging that wider implementation.

event.summary: Check whether removal of terminal-kind JSON breaks a browser tab running the preceding UI
event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. TLDR: A browser tab loaded before a helm upgrade might select an obsolete terminal renderer when the new session JSON omits terminal-kind fields. Source basis: assigned fixture/test patches remove agent_terminal, supervisor_creates_host_terminals and TabInfo.kind. SPEC_impl.md:495-504 and the HTTP contract test module docs state that browser tabs loaded before a helm upgrade keep running older decoders. Missing premise: whether the preceding UI requires those fields to choose the grid and whether the existing server/WebSocket boundary retires old clients. Suggested bucket: high if established as broken terminal UX; no security or loss-of-work route established. Confidence: uninvestigated source lead, not a finding. proposed_drop: false pending source checks. possible_cover: none searched. Could-be-highest: no established route; terminal rendering failure alone is not loss of owned work. Next checks: inspect parent-revision mirror defaults and terminal selection, new wire negotiation and browser reload/connection behavior, then close this lead under the same ID. No execution or reproduction requested or performed.

event.summary: Previous browser bundle misdraws after upgrade, explicitly accepted by the Grid streams contract
event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. TLDR: A browser tab left open across this upgrade can draw grid messages as terminal output and disconnect on input until reloaded. Investigation resolved the earlier lead by source and explicit specification acceptance. Source: parent-revision UI lib.rs:514-527 defaults omitted agent_terminal to None and supervisor_creates_host_terminals to false; session_view.rs:1755-1810 passes the resulting unknown kind to terminal.js through agent_spec_kind (:3839-3849). Parent assets/terminal.js:5718-5740 treats first binary data without a stream notice as bytes, and :5884-5930 only adopts the grid when a grid notice arrives. New helm terminal.rs:650-700 begins the outbound event pump without that notice; WS_PROTOCOL remains 'farhelm' in auth.rs:39. Contract and proposed_drop: SPEC_impl.md, Grid streams, :3021-3027 explicitly says: 'A page loaded from the previous helm and left open across the update must be reloaded; nothing keeps it working. Its terminals stop reconnecting on their own once the page sees the helm’s new build (the build-mismatch latch, which can take a few seconds), and any reconnect from it, automatic in that window or manual, misdraws the terminal: that page builds its old terminal component for a terminal whose kind the listing no longer names and takes the missing stream notice for an older helm’s byte stream, so it draws grid messages as terminal output, and what is typed into it ends the attachment as malformed input. Keeping the stream notice for such pages was considered and not done: a reload is the whole remedy.' (Typographic apostrophe normalized in this JSON quotation; repository text uses an ASCII apostrophe.) Suggested bucket: high/material UX if not accepted. Confidence: confirmed by source, not observed execution. possible_cover: this exact specification rule only; no other coverage searched. Could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work route; input is rejected as malformed, not established as an executed destructive command, and the remote session's owned work remains running. Caveats: JSON removal and stream-notice removal jointly produce the behavior; adjacent terminal transport is owned by another group. No tests or reproductions performed. Preserve the original suspected broken-terminal consequence; this candidate is excluded only because the governing specification expressly accepts it.
